en: Classified as a Text for Seating:
A Text for Seating According to the Vimalakīrti Sūtra I pay homage to the Tathāgata of Wondrous Joy,
the manifested form of the Fragrant Accumulation World in the upper direction.
Though he has a wife, children, and a retinue of kinsmen, his mind is pure and he constantly cultivates the holy life (*brahmacarya*).
His power of wisdom and supernormal faculties (*abhijñā*) are difficult to fathom; with his hand he shakes the sun and moon and moves Mount Sumeru.
Our Buddha, the Tathāgata, now resides in the grove, proclaiming the profound teaching of the Universal Assembly (*Samantabhadra-samudaya*).
The elder’s body and mind were filled with joy; Holding his precious parasol, he approached the Tathāgata.
Shaking it repeatedly, a cloud of golden bells was spread abroad; Pairs of the seven jewels and fragrances wafted afar, Until he reached the Dharma assembly within the garden enclosure.
There, holding up his precious parasol, he offered it to the Tathāgata.
Five hundred flower canopies stood before him; through the power of the Sage, they merged into a single canopy.
The sun, moon, and stars all appeared therein.
When the mountains, rivers, great earth, and the dragon palaces shook, the precious canopy shook; when the world moved, the precious canopy moved.
All the pure lands of the ten directions and all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time appear within them;
in the center of the land of Vaiśālī, amidst the brilliant and golden splendor of jewel trees,
there emerge many noble beings of compassionate nature who have long practiced the path in past lives.
The layman Vimalakīrti is the most honored among the assembly; his ten virtues are perfectly luminous, and he is revered by all.
Having drawn near to the boundless Buddhas of the three periods of time, he is thus titled the Elder Vimalakīrti.
Five hundred śrāvakas were all rebuked by him, as they had merely realized the emptiness of phenomena while abiding in the marks of existence.
Furthermore, there were the assemblies of Prabhāvyūha and Maitreya; Body and mind both prostrated among the disciples.
The True Gate of Non-duality is by nature harmonious;
Only Vimalakīrti, having personally realized awakening, Manifested illness within his chamber and lay alone, Extensively discoursing on the six inconceivable qualities.
The Great Sage Muni’s compassionate vows are profound;
he personally called each of the ten great assemblies one by one, yet all replied they were unable to inquire after his illness.
Only Mañjuśrī, the teacher of a thousand Buddhas, whose towering body moves within the Jewel Star Palace, with its lofty pearls swaying and precious seats flying, [approached].
Eighty thousand rishis fill the land with fragrance; a thousand times a thousand holy multitudes pervade the vast sky.
Invited to take their meal in the Fragrant Accumulation Hall of the Upper Realm, they transform seats and let out the lion’s roar of the Dharma King.
All arrive at the chamber of Vimalakīrti, where they perform their buddha-work in mutual proclamation.
This morning I intend to expound a most profound sutra; I pray that you will come here out of compassion to listen.
When the assembly hears this sutra, their sins shall be extinguished, And they shall all realize the Dharma-jewel body of Bodhi.
The burning house of saṃsāra is vast and boundless—when will it cease? The five desires ultimately give rise to the suffering of birth and death.
It is not as if one merely listens to the sutras seeking liberation; whether one can or cannot study the Buddha’s path and practice it, those who are able should remain reverent and join their palms.

Recite the titles of the sutras aloud, constantly lamenting that for many kalpas we have dwelt in saṃsāra, and that within this age of the Dharma’s decay there are many obstacles and difficulties. How shameful!
Acting as a boat for the Sahā world, you serve as the leader amidst the five turbidities.
You see only people creating evil and force them to gather together; when hearing the preaching of the sutras, they do not heed it as companions.
Having performed little merit in this life, it will be extremely difficult to find a human body in a future existence.
Unaware and unperceiving, one is busily preoccupied; Without fear or alarm, one perpetually creates transgressions.

If one does not encounter this Mahāyāna Sūtra today, It would be like seeing a single udumbara flower, Or encountering the crest-jewel of a Cakravartin King for a moment, Or finding the jewel within the garment of a destitute son—only today is it attained. The Ten Dharmas.
Since you have been able to come to this place of practice, you must surely wish to hear the subtle and wondrous Dharma.
O listeners seated below, do not be distracted; today the Dharma Master shall speak the truth.
Listen as he recounts how the Buddha first descended from Tuṣita Heaven to the human realm, first manifesting the signs of birth within the royal palace, whereupon nine dragons...
The Holy Sovereign Maya later went to the grove; the frequent queens and court ladies ran about in joyful clamor.
Fish leaped through the leaves of the Ashoka trees as they flourished in splendor; within that place, the Lady walked with graceful steps.
Raising her hand, she welcomed the descent of Śākyamuni, the Compassionate Father, who emerged from her left side into the womb. Nine dragons [attended].
The Rishi Asita addressed the Great King: "The auspicious signs of the Prince portend a future of perfect excellence.
Were it not for the virtuous bond established with Your Highness in a previous life, how could this humble servant now dare to take such liberty?
It is that he shall forever cast off worldly glory and wealth, wearying of the deep palace and becoming a Prince; he has renounced [all]."
For six years he practiced austerities in the mountains, dwelling among birds and beasts as his companions;
having endured long hunger, he attained realization beneath the Bodhi tree, subduing the hosts of Māra and achieving Perfect Enlightenment.

First, at Vulture Peak, he opened the way for the teachings to benefit all sentient beings; next, he expounded the doctrine of Emptiness to bring about awakening and understanding; and finally, toward...
On Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, the wondrous Dharma was expounded, benefiting the present and profiting the future; its inconceivable power is such that this morning I intend to preach this most profound sutra.

I only pray that out of compassion you will come here to listen; may the assembly, upon hearing this sutra, see their transgressions extinguished and vanish, and may they find peace within this ground of sorrow.
Having arrived at Chengnan, he did not return;
setting out early at dawn, he sought a sandy path,
and resting his journey at dusk, he sought provisions nearby.
Remembering the child and the mother, one should have long-term provisions;
one must see the Tathāgata within the assembly.
Today’s meritorious practice of expounding the sutra—
I pray that you may return early by way of the *páng* grass;
for this very place is where we part,
and every night one hears nothing but sorrow everywhere.
I ask you, why do you harbor such sorrow?
Yesterday, bandits seized my child.
I am solitary and poor, and in my old age I have met with such a fate.
I address the Yellow Heaven, praying that it will look upon me with favor.
If only mother and child may meet once more,
it would be like a withered tree sprouting branches again.
When my disciple was giving away even a single strand of thread, he made this vow:
"May the beautiful boy emerge early and dwell long;
may the sun set in this direction and shine in the west."
Do not say that when the sun sinks in the west, it ceases to exist;
here he enters extinction to transform other lands.
Do not say that the World-Honored One has truly passed into nirvana.
It is like the moon in the vast sky, obscured by drifting clouds so that it does not appear;
within the body, the Buddha-nature is exceedingly clear,
yet it remains entirely unmanifest, covered and hidden by karmic obstructions.
To cause the moon in the vast sky to appear, one must first rely upon a subtle, wild wind;
to attain the clarity of the Buddha-nature within one's own body, one must diligently listen to the Mahāyāna.
As soon as it is said that [the moon] has been blown away by the wild wind...
The moon’s reflection emerges from the vast sky;
there, one listens to the most profound and subtle Dharma.
Within the body, the Buddha-nature is exceedingly clear.
One drenching, two drenchings, three drenchings of rain;
it extinguishes how much dust in the streets!
One phrase, two phrases—the Mahāyāna Sūtra.
"I have extinguished much of the transgression within my body.
I intended to invite the Buddha, fearing that people might remain seated for too long;
thus, I intended to preach the sutra."
Whether wishing or not wishing, examine your mind and wait with palms joined;
in the West there is yet the Silver Terrace,
where the fourfold assembly listens to the Dharma and their minds are all opened.
May those who wish to hear the Dharma join their palms.
The *Dujiang* (Reciter) shall chant the title of the sutra.

Chanting the *Yazuo Wen* (Text for Seating) for the Lecture on the *Jiuwenshi Jing* (Bathhouse Sutra). Chanting the *Yazuo Wen* for the Lecture on the *Jiuwenshi Jing*. I prostrate before the Great Awakened Honored One of the Upper Direction.
I take refuge in the inconceivable and pure assembly, who,
through the four wisdoms and three bodies, respond to the vows of sentient beings;
I take refuge in Śākyamuni, sixteen feet tall, whose compassion is vast.
For hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, he served as a wheel-turning monarch,
yet took no pleasure in the affairs of royal palaces or matters of affection;
for thousands of millions of kalpas, he relinquished his life and relinquished his body.
Until this very body attains enlightenment,
one has long been submerged and mired in the ocean of birth and death;
unaware and unknowing, one is led away by the power of karma.
With defilements and obscurations eliminated, I now behold the Buddha;
his light illuminates the three thousandfold world system.
In the kingdom of Vaiśālī, there is a grove.
The woman is reborn within a loquat flower;
the branches and twigs of the jewel-tree possess a beautiful radiance.
This transformation-born body is neither ordinary nor holy.
Jīvaka returned and was born from the woman Nandā;
he was wondrously proficient in dharmic arts to save sentient beings,
able to cure all manner of illnesses so that everyone was healed.
The nation calls him a jewel, a Great King of Physicians.
His father’s name was Jīvaka, a man of compassionate virtue.
When he applied his needles, illnesses were instantly relieved.
Renowned throughout the eight kingdoms as an elder,
he returned from death to revive the dead within Jambudvīpa;
Jīvaka then called to mind the Honored Muni.
The Imperial Edict clearly commanded that all members of the household proceed to the Buddha.
They went directly to the Dharma assembly on Vulture Peak,
where they invited the Buddha and the ordinary monks to bathe.
The Buddha taught that each of the seven substances has its own efficacy;
it is not for the purpose of praying to bathe the Dharma-body.
Fragrant water can purify both ordinary beings and the assembly of sages.
Among those whose immeasurable merit fulfills all vows,
you are now prepared this morning to expound the most profound texts;
we pray that you will come here out of your compassion.
Upon hearing this sutra, the listeners' transgressions are extinguished;
they collectively realize the Dharma-jewel body of Bodhi.
This defiled and evil Jambudvīpa is truly pitiable.
Old and sick, I remain as if perpetually intoxicated throughout the day;
having already abandoned clamor to seek liberation,
I sit upright to listen to the sutras— whether I am capable or not.
Those who are capable should join their palms in reverent devotion;
chant forth the title of the scripture as it is brought forward.
